messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: problem: place an input$variable in SQL query
parts:
Hi Stratos, it looks like your renderTable code block is evaluating to a character vector, not a data frame. If you provide more code we may be able to help.

You also need to be very, very careful when integrating user input into your SQL queries. If your code looks like this:

sqlQuery(paste0("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = '", input$variable, "';"), ... )

then the user could type in something like

'; DELETE FROM users;

which would result in the sqlQuery call executing two SQL statements, the latter of which would erase all data from the users table. This is called a SQL injection attack and is one of the most commonly exploited security flaws in web applications.

The quick fix is to make sure that input$variable is SQL escaped. I'm not sure if RODBC provides an escaping function.

The better fix is to use parameterized queries, so the above would become:

sqlQuery("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?;", input$variable, ...)

but I don't think RODBC works that way (someone please correct me if I'm wrong).

Can anyone with some RODBC experience weigh in about the right way to do this?

Because of the problem with parameterized queries, I have switched to JDBC for shiny and other web-based applications. It's easy and amazingly fast. You must put the driver "sqljdbc4.jar" into you directory. Note that the dbSendPreparedQuery works for whole dataframes, and it is very fast. It also handles AutoIncrement columns, which always drops me back to by-row-Inserts in RODBC

library(RJDBC)
drv = JDBC("com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver", "sqljdbc4.jar")
con =  dbConnect(drv,"jdbc:sqlserver://localhost:64833;databaseName=MyDB",
          user = "user",password="mypassword")
vals = dbGetPreparedQuery(con, .... See documentation
As I said, I don't know if RODBC provides an escaping function, or a way to do parameterized queries.
